plotSections.title: The Journal and Gerk's Possible Importance
bullets: While the council of gods remains assembled, Sylan publicly reveals to Plymouth Gawater and the others why he believes Gerk is a uniquely important individual.

Sylan explains that years ago he found a handwritten journal containing two notable pieces of information: a search by the Navi for a child whose mother died while the child survived, and a plot against Sylan's family that later came to pass.

Following a spiritual experience in Jotunheim, Sylan became convinced that the child referenced in the journal is Gerk and believes Gerk is destined to act as a Keeper capable of opening the doors tied to the Keystones.
Plymouth carefully questions the source of Sylan's information, focusing on the journal's authorship, age, historical references, and whether it contains prophecy.
Plymouth recognizes the journal by reputation rather than by having personally read it and introduces the previously unknown concept of 'Mother's Prayer,' implying the journal may be connected to it.

plotSections.title: Gerk and the Mother's Prayer
bullets: Sylan revealed to Plymouth Gawater and the assembled gods that he believes Gerk is the child described in a journal he previously discovered and that Gerk is destined to become the keeper who will open the doors.
Sylan explained his conclusion comes from both the journal and a vision or meditation experienced in Jotunheim, where Gerk was identified as the child.
Plymouth questioned Sylan carefully about the journal's provenance, whether it was handwritten, whether it contained dates, and whether it explicitly referenced any prophecy.

Sylan clarified the journal itself only mentioned a child whose mother died while the child survived, along with a plot that ultimately led to the death of Sylan's family, but did not explicitly contain a prophecy.

Plymouth connected Sylan's story to an existing prophecy known as the Mother's Prayer (or Mother's Prophecy), suggesting the journal is associated with a known legendary tradition rather than an isolated account.
Dana recited the prophecy previously heard repeatedly within the Stronghold, allowing Plymouth to confirm it as the Mother's Prayer.

After hearing Sylan's interpretation, Plymouth personally examined Gerk, treating the claim with serious interest and attempting to determine whether Gerk truly is the individual referenced by the Mother's Prayer.

plotSections.title: Reaction of the Gatekeepers
bullets: The gathering remained in diplomatic session while the timeless gods continued their council, reinforcing that such meetings can last for years from a mortal perspective without inconveniencing the gods.
Juten Prime remained quiet, observing the discussion, while Elrus and Araden appeared restless.
Kit Anger became noticeably attentive once Sylan began discussing the journal and moved closer to observe Gerk after hearing the claim.

plotSections.title: The Mother's Prayer and Gerk's Role
bullets: The party recites the full text of the Mother's Prayer (also called the Mother's Prophecy), which had previously echoed throughout the stronghold.
Sylan explains his belief that Gerk is the child described in the Mother's Prayer and the keeper destined to open the doors.
Plymouth Gawater personally questions Gerk to determine whether he accepts the role described by the prophecy.
Gerk repeatedly explains that he has never considered himself a chosen hero and has simply been living his life, fighting alongside his friends, and doing what he believes is right.
Plymouth explains that the Mother's Prayer has long served as a sacred Navi prophecy used to identify individuals destined to play pivotal roles in Atlas' future.
According to Plymouth, the prophecy describes catastrophic events followed by a hero forced to make increasingly difficult choices, many of which Gerk has already begun facing.
Plymouth emphasizes that prophecy does not remove free will; Gerk's past decisions were always his own, and even the Mother's Tales can rewrite themselves if one of the chosen rejects their role.
Plymouth urges Gerk to consciously choose whether to embrace the prophecy rather than simply allowing events to happen to him.
After questioning, Gerk agrees that if accepting this role genuinely helps Atlas, he is willing to do so.

plotSections.title: Nature of the Chosen
bullets: Plymouth describes the Mother's Prayer as a great tree whose chosen individuals are its fruit, referring to them as sons and daughters of the Great Tree.
Plymouth reveals he has personally encountered three previous sons or daughters of the Great Tree: one accepted the calling while two rejected or abandoned it.
He warns that the current growing season is nearing its end and another bud will eventually grow if Gerk does not fulfill the role.
The Navi historically used the Mother's Prayer to identify individuals who would aid in exploring and protecting Atlas.
Plymouth states that this is the first time in roughly 1,500 years that someone has willingly stepped forward to assume the role described by the Mother's Prayer.

plotSections.title: The Party's Involvement
bullets: After Gerk accepts the role, Plymouth expands the discussion to the entire party.
He explains that the Mother's Prayer contains expectations not only for the chosen individual but also for the companions who travel beside them.
Participation remains entirely voluntary for the rest of the party, although Gerk's decision ultimately determines whether the prophetic path continues.
Plymouth stresses that the situation is extremely serious and cautions Gerk not to let the importance of his role inflate his ego.

plotSections.title: Gerk and the Mother's Prayer
bullets: A Navi elder questions Gerk about whether he truly wishes to continue the path laid before him and whether he genuinely desires the life he currently leads.
Gerk repeatedly states that he is happiest traveling with his friends, fighting, and continuing as he always has, regardless of whether the prophecy is true.
The Navi explain that the Mother's Prayer is an ancient Navi prophecy that has existed through many different written accounts by different authors, yet consistently tells the same core story.
The prophecy describes a catastrophic event followed by a hero who must make increasingly difficult choices. The speaker believes Gerk fulfills that role.

The prophecy does not dictate Gerk's past actions, only that he has arrived at this point. The Mother's Tales have even been observed rewriting themselves when a chosen individual abandons their path.

The Navi stress that accepting or rejecting the role is entirely Gerk's choice, but the opportunity is time-sensitive because the 'growing season' of the Great Tree is nearing its end and another chosen individual could emerge if Gerk refuses.
After questioning whether the prophecy truly refers to him, Gerk ultimately agrees to continue down the path if doing so will help Atlas.
The Navi celebrate Gerk's acceptance, noting that no chosen son or daughter has accepted the Mother's Prayer in roughly 1,500 years.

plotSections.title: The Great Tree and the Party's Role
bullets: The Mother's Prayer is compared to a fruiting tree, with each chosen hero being a fruit produced by the Great Tree.
Those chosen by the prophecy are referred to as sons and daughters of the Great Tree.
The Navi explain they have previously met three other chosen individuals: one accepted the responsibility while two abandoned it.
The rest of the party is offered the opportunity to voluntarily become Gerk's companions in the prophecy, symbolically becoming brothers and sisters alongside the chosen child of the Great Tree.
The choice is presented as entirely voluntary and affects only their participation in Gerk's prophetic role, not their existing friendships.
Walker, Glimmen, Dana, and the others express varying degrees of confusion before indicating they intend to stand with Gerk if he accepts the role.

plotSections.title: Acceptance of the Great Tree's Bond
bullets: Plymouth explains that Gerk is considered a son/child of the Great Tree and invites the rest of the party to formally join him as his companions, becoming metaphorical brothers and sisters to the Great Tree's chosen and relatives to its other children.
The party discusses the meaning of the invitation, with Walker and Glimmen admitting they do not understand the Great Tree or Gerk's connection to it.
Despite not fully understanding what they are agreeing to, every member of the party ultimately chooses to stand with Gerk and accept the invitation out of loyalty.
The ceremony has not yet begun by the end of the chunk; the party simply gathers and prepares to participate.

plotSections.title: Discussion of Daisy
bullets: Gerk again raises concerns about Daisy, the mysterious little blonde girl only he appears to notice.
Dana supports Gerk's claims, pointing out that flowers associated with Daisy appeared despite there being no flowers present, reinforcing that Daisy's presence was real.
Plymouth admits he has never personally seen Daisy and cannot explain her existence, but agrees the evidence is troubling enough that he intends to investigate further.

plotSections.title: The Mother's Prayer and the Doorman
bullets: Dana points out that the appearance of flowers confirms Daisy was present, as flowers are Daisy's signature, reinforcing that whatever Daisy is, she was recently here.
Plymouth Gawater gathers Gerk and the rest of the party, explaining that by standing with him they are voluntarily accepting the same responsibility tied to Gerk's destiny.

Plymouth reveals that the Eldarin Tree is a sacred Navi tree whose rings inspired the creation of the keystones. By studying and distilling those rings into the keystones, the Navi unintentionally began the Mother's Prayer prophecy.
The Mother's Prayer exists to preserve the health and prosperity of all Atlas, selecting individuals when needed to fulfill its purpose.
Plymouth explains that those chosen are metaphorically 'plucked' from the Eldarin Tree like ripe fruit and are entrusted with protecting Atlas rather than serving only the tree.
Gerk is offered the ancient title of Doorman of an Arch, becoming the first individual in many years to potentially hold the office.
The role of a Doorman is to open and close access to a specific Arch, maintain its connection, and protect it.
The rest of the party implicitly accepts that they are joining Gerk in supporting this responsibility.

plotSections.title: Choosing an Arch
bullets: Plymouth retrieves a keystone directly from one of the concentric circles in the floor and presents Gerk with the Keystone of Pitel.
Plymouth indicates that Gerk is not restricted to Pitel and implies he may choose which Arch's keystone he wishes to bear.
Before making a decision, Gerk turns to the rest of the party for advice on which Arch would be the best choice.
The party briefly reviews known properties of several Archs, including Pitel, Feldspar, Gilbrick, and Lith, but no final selection is made during this chunk.

plotSections.title: The Ceremony of the Doorman
bullets: Plymouth Gawater formally explains the true significance of Gerk's role as a 'Child of the Tree' before the assembled party, while Kit Anger, Juten Prime, Elrus, and Araden deliberately step back to allow the ceremony to proceed without interference.
The Eldarin Tree is revealed to be the sacred source from which the Navi derived the keystones by studying and distilling the tree's growth rings rather than carving them directly from wood.
The creation of the keystones unintentionally began the Mother's Prayer prophecy, which periodically chooses individuals to safeguard the prosperity of all Atlas.
Gerk accepts the responsibility of becoming the first Doorman in many years, a guardian empowered to open, close, protect, and steward an Arch rather than merely hide its keystone.
Plymouth explains that previous keepers were only charged with preserving keystones, while the new generation of Doormen are expected to actively improve and protect their assigned realms.

plotSections.title: Selection of the Keystones
bullets: Plymouth initially offers Gerk the keystone of Pitel, but Gerk learns he may freely choose which Arch to become Doorman of.
After discussing the various realms with his companions, Gerk chooses Midgar's keystone, which Walker had previously been carrying.
Plymouth formally entrusts Gerk with the Keystone of Midgar, emphasizing both its history and the greater responsibilities that now accompany it.
As Gerk accepts the keystone, white flower petals blow through the cavern and a mysterious feminine figure appears again, walking through empty space while leaving a trail of white flowers.
The party confirms they can all see the mysterious woman and flowers this time, although Plymouth appears more interested in completing the ceremony than investigating immediately.
Sylan is then offered and accepts stewardship of the Keystone of Gilbrick because of his connection to that realm.
Plymouth next offers Walker stewardship of the Keystone of La-rel, noting that Walker is the only member of the party not originally from Midgar.

plotSections.title: Keystone Assignments
bullets: Plymouth begins formally assigning the remaining keystones to members of the party, recognizing them as the new generation of guardians rather than merely keepers.
Plymouth explains that the previous keepers were only tasked with hiding and preserving the keystones, while the party's responsibility is to protect their realms and actively help them flourish.
Gerk accepts stewardship of Midgard's keystone.
Sylan accepts stewardship of Gilbrick's keystone.
Walker ultimately chooses stewardship of the Reach instead of his homeland of La-rel after reflecting on where he truly belongs.
Dana accepts stewardship of Pitel's keystone, calling it the center of the rings of Atlas.
Ord chooses Feldspar's keystone after considering the remaining options.

plotSections.title: The White Flower Figure
bullets: After Gerk accepts Midgard's keystone, a breeze carries white flower petals through the chamber.
Gerk sees the mysterious female figure walking away across the central void, leaving a trail of white flowers.
Unlike previous encounters, Sylan, Walker, and Plymouth all acknowledge that they can also see the mysterious figure.
Gerk suspects Plymouth may only be agreeing with him to keep him calm after successfully reading his behavior.
Plymouth encourages Gerk to complete the keystone ceremony first, implying that following the mysterious figure is a separate journey yet to come.

plotSections.title: Choosing a Realm
bullets: Walker debates whether to remain tied to La-rel, where he originated, or embrace the Reach as his true home.
Through a conversation with Glimmen, Walker concludes that his identity has changed and that protecting the Reach better reflects who he has become.
Glimmen expresses that she is content with either realm, noting both have become home in different ways.
Plymouth tailors each keystone assignment based on each person's background, history, or connection to a realm while allowing them to decline if they wished.

plotSections.title: Lith and Feldspar Clarified
bullets: Ord initially understands Lith as a realm that abandoned magic and lives in blissful ignorance.

Plymouth corrects this impression, explaining Lith has rejected conventional magic but possesses its own culture centered on folklore, cryptids, fairy tales, and misunderstood glimpses of the wider world.
Plymouth notes that a visibly magical individual like Ord would likely be viewed almost as a deity by the people of Lith rather than feared.

plotSections.title: Assignment of the Remaining Keystones
bullets: Walker decides that although La-rel was once his home, the Reach better represents who he has become. Glimmen supports his decision.
Plymouth entrusts Walker with the Reach keystone.
Dana accepts stewardship of the Pitel keystone, becoming guardian of the central arch of Atlas.
Ord chooses Feldspar after considering both Feldspar and Lith. Plymouth explains that Lith's people have not lost magic; instead they experience it through folklore, cryptids, and legends.
Ciri chooses Lith after hearing descriptions of the remaining available arches. Plymouth explains that Lith preserves magic through stories despite rejecting formal magic.

plotSections.title: The Remaining Keystones
bullets: After all party members make their choices, only the La-rel and Terov keystones remain unclaimed.
Plymouth says the original expedition had more members and that those absent companions should not be forgotten.
Kit Anger and the stewards of the Child of the Tree will safeguard the remaining keystones until new keepers arise.

plotSections.title: The Responsibility of the Keepers
bullets: Plymouth reminds the party that although they originally sought to protect the keystones from a lich, they are now personally responsible for safeguarding them.
He warns that the keystones are powerful artifacts and must never fall into the wrong hands.
Plymouth says he cannot tell the party exactly how to use the keystones, only guide them.
He hints that accepting stewardship of a keystone has changed each of them in a significant way.

plotSections.title: Keystone Assignments Completed
bullets: Ord formally accepts responsibility for protecting Feldspar and receives its keystone.
Plymouth finishes assigning the remaining keystones by explaining the responsibilities to Ciri.
Plymouth reiterates the party's individual assignments: Gerk protects Midgard, Sylan protects Gilbrick, Dana protects Pitel, Walker protects the Reach, Ord protects Feldspar, and Ciri chooses Lith.
Ciri chooses to become the keeper of Lith, completing the six player assignments while La-rel and Terov remain without mortal keepers.

plotSections.title: The Burden of the Keepers
bullets: Plymouth reminds the party that they originally began this journey with more companions and that the two unclaimed keystones should symbolize those who are no longer present.
La-rel and Terov will remain under the stewardship of Plymouth, Kit Anger, and the other children of the Great Eldarin Tree until worthy successors are found.
Plymouth emphasizes that they are only temporary stewards and intend to pass the keystones to future keepers when the time comes.
Plymouth warns that although the party sought to stop a lich, they now personally possess the artifacts the lich seeks, placing themselves in even greater danger.
The party is instructed to protect the keystones above all else, while Plymouth explains he cannot command how they use them but can only offer guidance.

plotSections.title: Children of the Great Eldarin Tree
bullets: Plymouth explains that by accepting the mantle of keystone keeper, each party member has become an honorary member of the Navi and a Child of the Great Eldarin Tree.
Kit Anger welcomes the party as brothers and sisters of the tree, formally acknowledging their new status.

plotSections.title: The Doorman Revealed
bullets: Plymouth clarifies that Gerk is uniquely the 'Doorman,' while the rest of the party are Gatekeepers.
Following Plymouth's instructions, Gerk instinctively grasps an invisible door handle and successfully opens a doorway through reality.
The doorway reveals a beach somewhere in Midgard, demonstrating Gerk's innate ability to create portals despite Plymouth having little understanding of how the power functions.
Sylan attempts to replicate the feat using his keystone but only briefly senses something before failing, suggesting the ability requires greater mastery.
Plymouth admits he is relying on ancient records because no one has exercised these abilities for centuries.

plotSections.title: Gerk's New Role as Doorman
bullets: Gerk is formally welcomed as an honorary member of the Navi and declared a 'Child of the Tree.'
Plymouth demonstrates that Gerk has gained the ability to open reality itself like a door, creating a portal to another location.
The first portal opens to an unknown beach on Midgard, confirming the ability functions but that even Plymouth does not yet understand how to control it.
Plymouth explains that Gerk's unique ability is what makes him the 'Doorman,' while the rest of the party are 'Gatekeepers.'
Sylan attempts to replicate the feat while holding a keystone but only briefly senses an unseen mechanism, suggesting the Gatekeeper abilities require practice or different conditions.

plotSections.title: Council of the Gods Concludes
bullets: With no further questions about Grixto, the party dismisses the assembled gods.
Vecna departs, remarking that he needs to find a book and warning the party not to get themselves killed because they are still mortal.
Ben opens his own doorway back to his traveling tavern and reminds the party they are always welcome.
Mahali follows Ben through the tavern door, inviting the party to return to the stronghold for a meal.
Narul silently departs after offering only a respectful nod and bow.
Emhet offers any final assistance before departing and leaves the party with advice for their new responsibilities as Gatekeepers.

plotSections.title: Emhet's Guidance
bullets: Emhet tells Dana to seek him through prayer if she requires additional guidance.
He warns the party that if 'the mind walks,' they should hold their breath, avoid shouting, and trust the path.
Emhet reminds the party that they now possess the keys and must fulfill their responsibilities as Gatekeepers.

plotSections.title: The Raven Queen's Warning
bullets: After every other deity leaves, the Raven Queen approaches the party alone.
As she nears, her terrifying harpy-like appearance resolves into the form of a regal woman wearing flowing black robes and a porcelain mask.
She acknowledges that the party has formed opinions about her but explains she understands mortals because she was once mortal herself.
She reveals she has witnessed some members of the party on the Everfalls, lingering specifically on Sylan and Dana.
She admits the party has exceeded her expectations, specifically expressing confidence in Sylan while saying Walker and Ord have begun to show more potential than she previously believed.
The Raven Queen offers to guide the party where they need to go but warns them not to waste either her time or their own.
She cautions the party against treating death lightly, reminding them that even bargains with death are limited.

She implies that some members of the party have very few chances remaining before ultimately encouraging them not to defy death, but instead to ensure their deaths have meaning when they eventually come.

plotSections.title: Farewells from the Deities
bullets: Ben departs by opening a doorway into his traveling tavern, reminding the party they are always welcome there and hinting that he will see some members sooner than others.
Mahali leaves with Ben, mentioning that if the party returns to the stronghold he plans to prepare a celebratory meal.
Narul silently bids the party farewell with a respectful nod and bow before departing.

Emhet offers the party one final chance to ask for assistance before leaving, reminds them that they now hold the keys, and warns: 'If the mind walks, hold your breath. Do not yell. Trust the path, gatekeeper.'

plotSections.title: The Raven Queen's Counsel
bullets: The Raven Queen approaches after the other deities depart, her appearance gradually shifting from a harpy-like form into a regal humanoid figure wearing a porcelain mask and flowing black robes.
She acknowledges that the party has formed opinions of her but says she understands mortals because she was once mortal herself.
She reveals she has walked the mortal world and has seen some members of the party upon the Everfalls, lingering particularly on Sylan and Dana.

She admits the party has exceeded her expectations, specifically expressing confidence in Sylan's resolve while noting that Walker and Ord have begun to show her more than she expected from ordinary mortals.
She agrees to guide the party where they need to go but warns them not to waste either her time or their own through foolish choices.
She emphasizes that death should not be treated carelessly, that every life has only so many chances, and encourages the party to make their lives meaningful rather than preparing for death.
When offering Sylan one final request, she accepts his decision not to ask anything further and instead reminds him to remember where he has been, value the life he has, and not live expecting death.
The Raven Queen reminds Sylan that he has been given a weapon and is 'a talon of my order, not a butcher,' emphasizing precision and purpose over indiscriminate killing.
After departing, her humanoid appearance transforms back into a shadowy harpy-like figure with large black wings as she flies away.

plotSections.title: Testing the Newly Acquired Keys
bullets: After the deities depart, the remaining allies include Glimmen, Juten Prime, Elrus, Araden, Boris, and Kit Anger.
The party begins experimenting with the newly acquired door-opening ability or keys.
Gerk repeatedly opens a doorway, finding that it initially leads to different random locations, including a rainy mountainside and later a quiet nighttime forest.
Dana suggests Gerk focus on a familiar destination such as the stronghold while opening the doorway.
Even after concentrating on the stronghold and making a Wisdom check, the doorway still opens to a different location, suggesting Gerk has not yet mastered control of the ability.

plotSections.title: Raven Queen's Farewell to Sylan
bullets: The Raven Queen declines to grant Sylan anything further after he chooses not to ask for another boon, respecting his decision.
She urges Sylan to remember his past and future, value what he has, and not live in expectation of death because no one knows when their life will end.
The Raven Queen reminds Sylan that he has been given a weapon and identifies him as 'a talon of my order, not a butcher,' emphasizing precision and purpose over indiscriminate violence.
After delivering her final guidance, the Raven Queen transforms, unfurling large black wings and departing down the corridor, leaving the party with their allies.

plotSections.title: Testing the Portal
bullets: After the Raven Queen departs, the party experiments further with Gerk's portal-opening ability.
Each attempt produces a different destination, suggesting the portal's destination is not yet under Gerk's full control.
One portal opens onto a rainy mountain landscape, while another reveals a dark forest illuminated by glowing insects.
Dana recognizes the forest's flora as matching the forests surrounding Langdale, suggesting the portal may have connected somewhere near the party's homeland.
Walker recognizes a distinctive tree from his previous travels near Langdale, reinforcing that the portal likely connected close to home.
The party prevents anyone from immediately walking through the portal, deciding they should first discuss the major responsibility they have just received before leaving.

plotSections.title: Processing Their New Responsibility
bullets: Sylan encourages the group to pause and process the significance of the new responsibility they have been entrusted with before acting on their newfound travel capability.
Plymouth Gawater expresses interest in understanding Walker's claimed ability to travel between realms, though Walker jokes instead of explaining.

plotSections.title: Returning Home
bullets: The party discovers that the portal appears to open into a forest with the same flora and fauna as the forests surrounding Langdale.
Dana recognizes the vegetation as matching the forests around the party's stronghold, though she cannot conclusively identify the exact location without traveling through the portal.
Walker recognizes a distinctive tree from his previous travels, confirming the portal leads somewhere in the vicinity of Langdale.
The party decides not to immediately leave through the portal, acknowledging they still have responsibilities to address before departing.

plotSections.title: Gerk's New Responsibility
bullets: Plymouth reminds Gerk that he is currently maintaining an extremely powerful portal between two locations.
Plymouth advises Gerk to close the portal, warning that while reopening it to the exact same destination may be difficult, leaving it open poses a greater risk.
Plymouth references previous incidents where open portals allowed dangerous creatures to enter, reinforcing the need for caution.
Plymouth implies he intends to teach Gerk more about safely controlling and reopening portals in the future.

plotSections.title: Processing Recent Events
bullets: The party takes time to process the major revelations and responsibilities they have recently acquired rather than immediately returning home.
Dana joins Kit Anger for a drink while the rest of the party relaxes and reflects on recent events.
Sylan spends time reviewing and recording notes from the Raven Queen's earlier conversation, recognizing its importance.
The group discusses eventually visiting Ben's traveling tavern once their immediate business is finished.

Gerk says he is happiest traveling with his friends and smashing things.

Gerk questions whether the prophecy could simply describe many different people.

Gerk agrees to continue pursuing the prophetic role if it helps Atlas.
The Navi announce that no one has accepted the Mother's Prayer in approximately 1,500 years.
The rest of the party is invited to voluntarily become Gerk's companions within the prophecy.
Walker and Glimmen express confusion about what the Great Tree means.
Dana states she will continue following Gerk because she believes there is purpose behind his selection.
Gerk again brings up the mysterious girl Daisy, expressing concern that no one else seems to know who she is despite her seemingly supernatural abilities.
Plymouth explains that Gerk is a child of the Great Tree and offers the rest of the party the opportunity to formally join him.
Walker and Glimmen privately admit they do not understand what the Great Tree is or what Plymouth is describing.
The party jokes about Gerk receiving a crown and about becoming members of the Great Tree's family.
Dana declares that wherever Gerk goes, she will follow, trusting there is a purpose if he has been chosen.
Gerk asks whether anyone else has figured out who Daisy is.
Plymouth states he has never seen Daisy despite Gerk mentioning her several times previously.
Dana confirms that flowers connected to Daisy appeared when no flowers should have existed, convincing her Daisy truly was present.
Plymouth acknowledges the situation is troubling and says he will review his notes regarding Daisy.
Plymouth asks the party to step forward if they wish to join Gerk.
Ciri rejoins the group after hiding in the shadows.
After confirming what the invitation means, Walker, Ord, Sylan, Dana, Ciri, and the rest of the party all step forward to stand with Gerk.
The party assembles around Gerk, preparing for the ceremony to begin.
Dana concludes Daisy was recently present because flowers, Daisy's signature, appeared around Gerk.
Plymouth asks Gerk and the rest of the party to step forward if they wish to participate in Gerk's calling.
Walker, Dana, Ord, Sylan, and Ciri all agree to stand with Gerk.
Kit Anger and Juten Prime intentionally step back to observe without interfering.
Plymouth explains the significance of the Eldarin Tree to the Navi.
Plymouth reveals the keystones were created from the knowledge of the Eldarin Tree's rings.
Plymouth explains that creating the keystones unintentionally initiated the Mother's Prayer prophecy.
Plymouth tells Gerk he can become the first Doorman of an Arch in many years.
Plymouth explains that a Doorman opens, closes, connects to, and protects an Arch.
Plymouth retrieves the Keystone of Pitel and offers it to Gerk.
Gerk learns he may choose which Arch he wishes to represent and asks his companions for advice.
The party begins discussing the characteristics of the various Archs while considering Gerk's choice.
The party assembles around Gerk as the keystone ceremony begins.
Kit Anger, Juten Prime, Elrus, and Araden intentionally refrain from interfering with the ceremony.
Plymouth explains the history of the Eldarin Tree and its connection to the Navi.
Plymouth reveals that the keystones were created by studying and distilling the rings of the Eldarin Tree.

Plymouth first presents Gerk with the Keystone of Pitel.
Gerk consults the party before making his decision.
Gerk chooses to become the Doorman of Midgar.
Walker returns the Midgar keystone to Plymouth, who formally presents it to Gerk.
